newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila oil prices seen rising by 30 centavos/litre.
newsitem.headline: Manila oil prices seen rising by 30 centavos/litre.

text.p: The Philippines' Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) said on Tuesday it expected petroleum product prices to be raised by an average of 30 centavos per litre late this week.

ERB Chairman Bayani Faylona told Reuters that initial computations showed the price of premium gasoline would be raised by 35 centavos per litre, while unleaded gasoline would be raised by 34 centavos. Regular gasoline prices could increase by 33 centavos per litre.
Faylona said fuel oil prices will rise by 21 centavos, liquefied petroleum gasoline by 23 centavos and diesel by 44 centavos per litre.
Jet fuel or aviation turbo would also be raised by 11.99 centavos per litre, Faylona added.

Faylona said the increases in Singapore Posted Prices (SPP) would lead to the increase in domestic pump prices. The SPP is the basis of the monthly automatic oil price formula used by the ERB to adjust petroleum prices in preparation for full deregulation next year.
"We will most probably make the final announcement on Thursday or Friday as we are waiting for Singapore prices to soften," said Faylona.
Under the oil industry deregulation law, Faylona said the ERB was mandated to adjust oil prices using the automatic oil price formula on or before every third Monday of the month.
The adjustment this week will be the fourth since the government implemented the formula in August as part of the partial deregulation of the oil industry.
Last month, the ERB raised oil prices by an average of 30.72 centavos, the highest since August.
